video_title: Why Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla doesn’t like being called a Champion | CHAMPION MINDSET

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the thin line between genius and insanity
quotes.excerpt: There's such a small space between genius and insanity. There's such a small space between champion and ultimate failure.
quotes.quote: I think what defines success is can you surrender to the fact that you might fail along the way. There's such a small space between genius and insanity. There's such a small space between champion and ultimate failure. Like it's not this, it's like this.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the difficulty of winning an NBA championship
quotes.excerpt: Championships are not won in one year. You don't win a belt in one match.
quotes.quote: Championships are not won in one year. You don't win a belt in one match.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the reality of the NBA season
quotes.excerpt: At the end of the season, only one team wins and then 29 lose.
quotes.quote: At the end of the season, only one team wins and then 29 lose. And so you get 29 justifications, and on those 29 different justifications as to where part of those justifications of like, well, we had a good regular season, well, we were this, well, we weren't supposed to be this. And you know, along the journey, you have to balance the justifications versus the expectation and the standard of winning.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the influence of his father, Dan Mazzulla
quotes.excerpt: My dad just set the standard and set the tone from day one.
quotes.quote: My dad just set the standard and set the tone from day one. He set the tone as far as whatever you do, you're going to do it with a level of physical toughness and a level of mental toughness. And it came with a lot of success, but it came with a lot of pain along the way. And throughout my life, I had to learn how to navigate some of those scars and some of those things, but I wouldn't be here without him, and I wouldn't be here without the mentality that he put into our family.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on why he needed his father's tough coaching
quotes.excerpt: You go through life and you're always asking yourself what you want, but the question is what you need.
quotes.quote: You go through life and you're always asking yourself what you want, but the question is what you need more than what you want. And that's what I needed, and that's what he felt like what was best at the time. And so there were moments of our life where we were father-son, but I always felt he had a pulse on I'm doing this for the long term. I'm doing this because I've been there. He played college basketball, he played professional basketball, he has seen what success looks like.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the importance of emotional intelligence in parenting
quotes.excerpt: The piece that he neglected a little bit was emotional intelligence.
quotes.quote: With my kids now, I think the piece that he neglected a little bit was emotional intelligence. I didn't know how to leverage the scars that he left or the trauma that I may have felt from certain things, and so I didn't know how to handle that. And where I get better is I try to treat my kids that way, but also apply the emotional intelligence aspect to it.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the challenge of raising kids with everything
quotes.excerpt: They have everything, and so you have to find ways to deprive them.
quotes.quote: They have everything, and so you have to find ways to deprive them. And whether you deprive them mentally, deprive them emotionally, psychologically, you just have to find moments for it. But I also think that gratitude is something that we talk about a lot as a family. I think God has given us all opportunities, different gifts, and different abilities, and we got to use those. And so I think, and that's something I didn't learn when I was younger, is you can leverage gratitude.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on his time playing for Bob Huggins
quotes.excerpt: Huggins comes and he was the exact coach that I needed at the time.
quotes.quote: I had Coach B-Line first, so I went there, and he was great, but you know, he went to Michigan. And I remember calling him, and he was like, you're not leaving. So like, you're not transferring, you're staying there. I don't really care who the coach is. He never let me transfer out of high school, he never let like, you know, he was just like, you picked that place, that's where you're going. You got to figure it out. So Huggins comes and he was the exact coach that I needed at the time. He was an exact replica of my dad, with the ability to, you know, push you to a level that you didn't think you could get to, but at the same time have timely moments of love.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the Celtics' physical style of play
quotes.excerpt: We played mostly under fear. And that's necessary from time to time.
quotes.quote: We played mostly under fear. And that's necessary from time to time. I'm not sure it's a long standing sustainable thing, but like we played out of fear a lot of the times. And Huggins was always like, I'd rather you take it out, like be so mad at me, take it out on the other team.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on losing his identity as a player
quotes.excerpt: I lost myself, and I think that was the first time in my life where I wasn't Joe Mazzulla.
quotes.quote: I lost myself, and I think that was the first time in my life where I wasn't Joe Mazzulla the basketball player. Like I wasn't the project that my dad was working on, you know, like I wasn't. And so I lost myself for a while, but I had great people around me. But it goes back to one of those things, like this is what I need to do. Like I don't, I think we have to find a way in life to like, simulate situations where you don't have a choice.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the importance of his team trainer
quotes.excerpt: The guy who drove me to my shoulder surgery my junior year is the guy that sits right next to me.
quotes.quote: The guy who drove me to my shoulder surgery my junior year is the guy that sits right next to me on the bench now. And so I'm forever indebted to him because like, he, I didn't personally, it just happened. But the guy who drove me to my shoulder surgery my junior year is the guy that sits right next to me on the bench now. And so it's people like that that, you're I'm here because of people like him. I'm here because the people around me make sure I didn't become a screw-up.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on his emotional release through sports
quotes.excerpt: Everything about me was sports, sports, sports, basketball, basketball, basketball.
quotes.quote: Everything about me was sports, sports, sports, basketball, basketball, basketball. Like you got to do it. And when it got, it was the first time in my life that had gotten taken away. Because there were some other injuries that I had and my dad was like, no, like you you just have to play. But this one I couldn't. So yeah, I mean I was, I didn't have an emotional release, yeah.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on his role as a captain and leader
quotes.excerpt: I was the point guard and I was the senior and so I became kind of ex-officio one of the captains.
quotes.quote: I was the point guard and I was the senior and so I became kind of ex-officio one of the captains. But I think, but that doesn't mean you're the best player. I think that's where people get confused. It's like, no, it's the person that can lead. So but it came with a lot of, uh, you know, I think self-awareness. I was probably one of the worst players on the team and I knew that, but I knew where to get the ball to, you know, and I knew how to stay out of the way and I knew what my role was and, you know, I didn't start, didn't finish sometimes.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the importance of surrounding yourself with good people
quotes.excerpt: I'm only who I am because of the people I'm around.
quotes.quote: I'm only who I am because of the people I'm around. It's my wife, my kids, my staff, the players, and like the people you surround yourself with. It took me a while, but I think that's the most important thing.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the lesson that winning is different
quotes.excerpt: That was the first lesson of like, winning is different.
quotes.quote: That was the first lesson of like, winning is different. That was the first time where we were on the big stage and, and, and, um, to me, witnessing what Duke did was like, no, no, that's winning. You know, and that's, that's what I was like, okay, like it takes something different to really win.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on his transition to coaching
quotes.excerpt: The year I got hurt and I was sitting on the bench.
quotes.quote: The year I got hurt and I was sitting on the bench. And I was very lucky, Coach Hugs let me in on the coaches' meetings. Um, I did a couple scouts, I learned the video. I had to stay engaged because again, I was, you know, teetering, losing myself emotionally and so the coaching staff did a great job keeping me engaged. I also saw the game differently, you know, because you're able to take a 30,000-foot view out.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the importance of having a great coach
quotes.excerpt: I'm not going to name them all, but I can name almost every single coach I had.
quotes.quote: I'm not going to name them all, but I can name almost every single coach I had from fifth grade CYO to Coach Huggins at West Virginia. And I can tell you the things that they taught me. I can even write up some of the practice plans. I've never had a bad experience.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on learning from better players
quotes.excerpt: I just copycatted the people who were better than me.
quotes.quote: I just copycatted the people who were better than me. I mean, I think that's, I don't know if, uh, you know, I don't mind saying that. Like I, I, I, I think I learned most about my dad once he died. I think I became a better father, uh, when he passed. I think I understood what he was doing more once he passed. And I think that's part of the reason, you know, why God it was time was for us to learn the things that we needed to learn.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the importance of patience in coaching
quotes.excerpt: You have to have a gift of, you have to be given patience.
quotes.quote: You have to have a gift of, you have to be given patience. So like, uh, I'm very grateful to the people that I've worked for that they've allowed me to, um, execute the vision that we have as a process, you know, because some coaches don't get, uh, three, four, five years to be able to, you know, uh, go about their vision and process.

quotes.speaker: Joe Mazzulla
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla on the importance of self-awareness and self-development
quotes.excerpt: There's a significant like difference but they're so minuscule as you're on your journey.
quotes.quote: There's a significant like difference but they're so minuscule as you're on your journey, you know, white belt to blue belt to this to champion and, you know, then you lose the belt, then you have to get the belt back. Like, you know, there's there's stuff to be learned from individual sports that you can apply to team sports and I think it the the biggest things are like the small things between winning and losing. How do you, you know, take on, uh, winning the belt but then defending it, then losing it and then having to get it back.
